raw.assessment: The incumbent preserved every ordered design, and unadjusted small covers took 25–31 minutes, within the time target (H2-O5, H2-O6). Reopening seams occurred in five of eight large covers, two of fourteen medium covers, and no small covers (H2-O1, H2-O2), supporting investigation of size-dependent fit without establishing its cause. Rounded customer-table corners absent from reference tables are a concrete limitation: both observed installation failures involved them (H2-O3). Passing the reference check therefore cannot establish customer fit. Wash width changes, confounded production variables, and actual area waste remain unresolved; the previous 37-minute median and ten installations do not establish next-batch success.

openings.claim: The common cutting allowance may create a systematic finished-dimension error that increases with table size, contributing to large-cover seam rework.
openings.delta: Test the allowance before committing the whole batch to cutting.
openings.prediction: Signed finished-dimension errors will increase consistently with size; errors varying chiefly with operator, direction, or design would weaken this account.
openings.probe: Make early ordered covers across the three sizes within an area-checked batch cutting layout. Record cut and sewn dimensions, operator, design, direction, fitting corrections, and working time. Measure retained samples in both axes through the stipulated wash test. Trial a revised allowance only if errors support it; verify cover wash survival and total cutting waste.
assumptions: Trials, measurement, and any revision fit the 350-unit budget and three-week window; this needs checking.

openings.claim: Does corner geometry cause customer fitting failure independently of tabletop length and width?
openings.delta: Distinguish reference-table conformity from fit on the specified customer table.
openings.prediction: If corner geometry matters independently, covers with matching length and width will still seat differently on rounded and square corners.
openings.probe: Request length, width, and corner measurements from the six willing customers, prioritizing nominal-dimension orders where available. Compare placement and pocket interference for similar-size tables with different corners before changing pocket geometry. Any revision must preserve ordered size/design, tool-free removal, wash performance, and the area-waste limit.
assumptions: Comparable tables or measurements are available; otherwise the geometry effect remains unresolved.

raw.assessment: The observations locate fitting problems but do not establish their causes. Two speculative capabilities could reduce adjustment; neither presently demonstrates the 38-of-40 first-placement target, wash durability, or 32-minute median.

openings.claim: A geometry-to-pattern transfer rule could produce the required finished fit from actual tabletop dimensions, corner shape, cloth direction, and measured wash change.
openings.delta: Replace the common allowance and whole-batch cutting with a measured pilot and a validated cutting card before releasing similar orders for cutting.
openings.prediction: If geometry and dimensional change explain the failures, corrected patterns should reduce measured fit error on a table withheld from calibration; failure despite accurate geometry would weaken this explanation.
openings.probe: Presently test the partial capability: obtain actual dimensions and corner measurements from the six willing customers; measure both cloth axes on retained offcuts through the stipulated wash test. Calibrate a paper correction rule on reference-table pilots, then assess an independently measured table configuration before further cutting. Record working time and calculate cutting waste by area.
assumptions: Table measurements can be reproduced on available references or an affordable temporary fixture.
A small pilot predicts later seam and cloth behavior.
Pilots remain usable stock; total changes stay within 350 units and three weeks, with at most 8% area waste.

openings.claim: Hidden compliant corner pockets could let a cover self-seat across a bounded range of corner shapes while keeping the ordered printed surface positioned.
openings.delta: Absorb corner mismatch mechanically instead of requiring exact corner-pattern matching.
openings.prediction: At equal tabletop dimensions, compliant pockets should improve rounded-corner seating relative to existing pockets without shifting the visible design; improvement only after changing dimensions would weaken the compliance hypothesis.
openings.probe: Build one retained-offcut pocket with an enclosed washable elastic segment and compare seating, slip, and removal against an existing pocket across measured corner profiles, before and after five wash cycles. Time construction before committing batch cloth.
assumptions: Elastic travel and tension can accommodate measured corners without puckering.
Matching offcuts and affordable elastic suffice.
Full-cover validation preserves design, tool-free removal, budget, deadline, and area-waste limit.

openings.claim: Common allowance may cause size-dependent finished-dimension error.
openings.discriminator: Signed error increases with size rather than operator, direction or design.
openings.probe: Early usable covers across sizes: record cut/sewn dimensions, confounders, corrections and time; wash retained samples in both axes. Revise allowance only if supported.

openings.claim: Corner geometry may impair fit independently of tabletop dimensions.
openings.discriminator: Different seating at equal length/width with rounded versus square corners.
openings.probe: Obtain six customers’ dimensions/corners, prioritizing nominal orders where available; compare pocket interference before revision.
openings.uncertainty: Comparable tables may be unavailable; reference fit cannot establish customer fit.

openings.claim: A measured geometry-to-pattern rule could integrate dimensions, corners, direction and wash change.
openings.discriminator: Corrected patterns reduce fit error on a withheld table configuration.
openings.probe: Use customer measurements and two-axis wash samples; calibrate reference-table pilots, validate independently before releasing similar orders; record time and area waste.
openings.uncertainty: Reproducible fixtures, usable pilots and transfer to later production unproven.

openings.claim: Hidden compliant pockets could absorb bounded corner variation while preserving visible design.
openings.discriminator: Better seating at equal dimensions without design shift.
openings.probe: Compare offcut enclosed-elastic and existing pockets across measured corners: seating, slip, removal before/after five washes; time construction before batch commitment.
openings.uncertainty: Travel, tension, puckering, cost and full-cover performance unproven.

post_distill.decision: Probe before whole-batch cutting. All changes require ordered sizes/designs, purchased stock, <=8% area waste, five-cycle durability, tool-free removal, existing two machines, <=350 units and three weeks. Success remains unproven: >=38/40 first placements, all designs correct, median work <=32 minutes.
